payload.title: FIX-SQLITE-DOCKER-VIRT-CORRUPTION

occurrences.evidence: multiple market.db.corrupt-* backup files in volume dated 2026-04-25

occurrences.incident: market.db SQLITE_CORRUPT restart-loop in mcp-server, pages 107935–107973 corrupted
occurrences.mechanism: Container reapZombieJobRuns UPDATE crashed on cron_job_runs; PRAGMA integrity_check showed widespread corruption across Trees 8772, 57970, 57984, 49348. No code regression (image SHA 1c5845d64406, unchanged 42h). Recovery: DB swap from 04:30Z backup (PRAGMA integrity_check=ok), container healthy post-swap.
occurrences.concurrent_activity: dev-team peer agent (BOUNDED-1 HPG-DISCOVER-CONSOLIDATED-PDF, 15:29Z) may have exec-written live DB during vulnerable window (15:41–15:44Z corruption window)

payload.diagnosis: Two SQLITE_CORRUPT incidents (2026-04-25, 2026-07-13) indicate a recurring Docker virtualization layer corruption pattern, not application-code regression. Root cause likely: (a) concurrent exec-write from peer container + Docker virt race condition, (b) WAL checkpoint timing vulnerability, or (c) Docker named-volume sync issue under concurrent load. Corruption is not localized to operational telemetry (cron_job_runs) — it spreads across unrelated page ranges, suggesting a low-level FS/virt corruption rather than an application invariant violation.
payload.suggested_fix: Hardening options: (1) Add per-transaction write-lock coordination (currently multiple containers can exec-write same DB); (2) Enforce WAL checkpoint synchronization before peer exec-writes; (3) Switch to SQLite replication/RAFT-based consensus (distributed, corruption-resistant); (4) Implement periodic integrity-check health gates (PRAGMA integrity_check every N hours, alert if FAIL). Scope/feasibility assessment left to architect and infrastructure team.
payload.verification_gate: architect assessment doc addressing root-cause hypothesis and hardening feasibility; ops will not attempt application workarounds without architecture guidance (recurring-bug escalation means human decision required)
